verdict.rationale: Modal Sandboxes are documented as isolated containers/VMs for running untrusted or agent code, with networking controls (block_network, CIDR/domain allowlists) that can restrict outbound access, which supports keeping host secrets/credentials unreachable. However, there is no explicit documentation describing secret-isolation guarantees or how host credentials are prevented from leaking into the sandbox (e.g., environment variable scoping, explicit secret injection controls) — the evidence focuses on general network/process isolation rather than credential-specific security claims. missing for 10: explicit documentation on how host secrets/credentials are excluded or scoped from sandbox environments, independent security audit or hands-on validation of secret isolation, and any first-party statement on credential handling policy.
